DATED: 18/09/2023  
 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION NO. 6875 of 2022 ==========================================================
 HIMALAY CHANDRAKANT PARMAR  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT ==========================================================
Appearance:
A S TIMBALIA(7372) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 NOTICE SERVED for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MR RONAK RAVAL, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE M. R. MENGDEY  Date : 18/09/2023  ORAL ORDER 1. RULE.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Learned APP waives service of rule for the respondent-State.

2. The present application has been filed by the applicant - original accused under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking quashing and setting aside the impugned FIR being I.C.R.No.11210064220452 of 2022 registered with Godadara Police Station, Surat for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code (herein after referred to as the "IPC").

3. Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that the present applicant and the prosecutrix were in consensual relationship and as part of the said consensual relationship, physical relationship was established between them on several occasions.

However, thereafter, since the prosecutrix wanted to NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6875/2022 ORDER DATED: 18/09/2023 undefined marry the present applicant to which the applicant was not agreeable, the relationship between them got strained and that is why the prosecutrix has lodged the present FIR.

Himalay Chandrakant Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147227947/
1 4.

entities.text: Himalay Chandrakant Parmar vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that upon bare perusal of the FIR in question itself, it appears that the relationship between the applicant and the prosecutrix were consensual.
Thus, present FIR has been lodge with an ulterior motive.
He, therefore, submitted to allow the present application by quashing and setting aside the impugned FIR mentioned herein above.

5. Learned APP for the respondent-State has vehemently opposed the present application, inter alia,
contending that the physical relationship was established between the applicant and the prosecutrix only because the present applicant had promised her to marry with her and subsequently, the applicant had retracted from the said promise and thus, had cheated the prosecutrix.

He, therefore,
submitted that there is a prima facie case against the present applicant for the offence alleged in the FIR.
He, therefore, submitted to dismiss the present application.
6. Though served, none appears for the respondent no.2.
7. Heard learned advocates for the parties and perused the material available on record.
In the impugned FIR itself, the first informant has mentioned that she had earlier married to somebody else and had divorced her earlier husband.
The applicant and the first informant were working together and were known to each other since long.

The fact of her divorce was NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6875/2022 ORDER DATED: 18/09/2023 undefined brought by her to the notice of the present applicant, and thereafter, the present applicant used to regularly visit her house and physical relationship was established between them.

One year prior to the FIR, the present applicant had applied Sindur on her head and had also given a Mangalsutra to her, and thereafter, also, they were regularly establishing the physical relationship.
This fact indicates that the physical relationship was established between the present applicant and the prosecutrix with her consent.
However, subsequently, it appears that the prosecutrix wanted to marry with present applicant to which the applicant was not agreeable.
The same appears to have triggered the dispute between them, which has resulted into filing of the present FIR.

8. Upon bare perusal of the FIR, it is clear that the present applicant and the prosecutrix were known to each other for quite some time and on several occasions, the sexual relationship between them was established with the clear consent of the prosecutrix.
It is a case on behalf of prosecutirx that the present applicant had promised her to marry with her and subsequently, the applicant had retracted from the said promise.
It is required to be noted at this stage that the prosecutrix was adult when she came into contact with the present applicant.
From the record, it appears that the applicant and the prosecutrix came into contact in the Year-2013 and since then both of them appeared to be indulging in sexual relationship.

9. Having regard to the age of the prosecutrix at the time of incident and also having regard to the fact that the prosecutrix was a divorcee from her earlier marriage, it is hard to believe NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/6875/2022 ORDER DATED: 18/09/2023 undefined that she would consent the present applicant for sexual relationship upon promise of marriage.

The Apex Court in its recent decision in case of Naim Ahmed Vs. State (NCT of Delhi) reported in 2023(244) AIC 119 has observed as under:-
Himalay Chandrakant Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147227947/
2 "In case of false promise, the accused right from the beginning would not have any intention to marry the prosecutrix and would have cheated or deceited the prosecutrix by giving a false promise to marry her only with a view to satisfy his lust,
whereas in case of breach of promise, one cannot deny a possibility that the accused might have given a promise with all seriousness to marry her, and subsequently might have encountered certain circumstances unforeseen by him or the circumstances beyond his control, which prevented him to fulfill his promise so, it would be a folly to treat each breach of promise to marry as a false promise and to prosecute a person for the offence of rape under Section 376 IPC."
10.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid aspects, the present application is allowed.

The impugned FIR being I.C.R.No.11210064220452 of 2022 registered with Godadara Police Station, Surat for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) of the IPC as well as all other consequential proceedings arising out of the aforesaid F.I.R are hereby quashed and set aside.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
Direct service permitted.

(M. R. MENGDEY,J) GIRISH Himalay Chandrakant Parmar vs State Of Gujarat on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147227947/
